reason: E1 directly supports oxide formation and enhanced corrosion/wear resistance after 800 °C air exposure, but the cited evidence does not address the predicted monotonic decrease in wear rate with time/temperature, nor does it cover the 500–800 °C range or the specific loading conditions. E3 supports oxide lubrication under high load but for a different alloy (CoCrFeMnNi) and without thermal pre-exposure.
premises: Thermal exposure of FeNiCrCoCu coating in air at 800 °C forms a protective Cr2O3 and (Fe,Co,Ni,Mn,Cu)3O4 oxide layer
This oxide layer enhances corrosion and wear resistance
Wear rate decreases with increasing thermal exposure time and temperature due to a thicker, more stable oxide
Oxide formation on worn surfaces under high load reduces friction coefficient and specific wear rate
